controls: Guard the vector path with __riscv_v && __riscv_zvfhmin and keep the current scalar decode_fp16 loop as the untouched fallback, following the extension-macro-guard rule.

Choose source LMUL so VLMAX(e16) covers a practical batch (e.g. e16m1 = 8 elems on zvl128b) and the e32 destination register group fits, with a stable vtype (one vsetvl per iteration, no reconfig inside the loop).
Follow the kernel-conventions widening rule for source/destination LMUL budgets.
Gate enabling on the exhaustive 0x0000..0xFFFF bit-pattern comparison passing against decode_fp16.
reasons: Widening conversion doubles the destination register group (e16m1 -> e32m2); with VLEN=128 the chosen LMUL must keep the e32 destination within the register file and not force spills.

vfwcvt.f.f.v NaN quieting/payload rules may differ from decode_fp16's bit-preserving infnan path (o + 0x70000000), which would change reconstruction bits and sql2_recons_error even when numerically close.
Reconstruction feeds faiss distance computations; any bit-level drift changes sq-accuracy results, so the vector path must be validated exhaustively before enabling.
Gating on __riscv_v alone is wrong: vfwcvt.f.f.v requires zvfhmin; improper gating yields a compile error or illegal instruction.
vsetvl and pipeline fill overhead wins only when d is not tiny; a threshold or dispatch must avoid regressing short vectors.

conditions.description: Runtime exposes v + zvfhmin (build ISA already tags v1p0+zvfhmin, zvl128b; verify via /proc/cpuinfo or hwprobe before relying on the tag).
decode_vector must remain bit-identical to the scalar decode_fp16 reference for every FP16 bit pattern the consumer can produce.
d is large enough to amortize one vsetvl and vector load/store per vector (benchmark QT_fp16 uses code_size=256 bytes, i.e. d=128; worst realistic d for this template is the quantizer's d).

actions.proposal: Add an RVV fast path to QuantizerFP16 decode_vector gated on __riscv_v && __riscv_zvfhmin: per iteration vsetvl_e16m* on remaining count, vle16 load of FP16 codes, vfwcvt.f.f.v widening FP16->FP32 (native IEEE handling of normals, denormals, ±0, ±Inf, NaN), vse32 store, with tail handling for d % VL and the existing scalar decode_fp16 loop retained as the fallback; add a masked/narrow repair only if bit-exact NaN-payload/sNaN parity with decode_fp16 is required.

correctness_checks: Exhaustively compare vector decode against decode_fp16 for all 65536 FP16 bit patterns, covering ±0, sNaN/qNaN with varied payloads, ±Inf, largest/smallest normals, subnormals.
Re-run the sq-accuracy benchmark and confirm sql2_recons_error and ndiff_for_idempotence are unchanged.
Build with and without the zvfhmin/v tags and confirm the vector build emits vfwcvt.f.f.v in decode_vector while the fallback build matches the previous scalar disassembly.
Perf-annotate decode_vector before/after to confirm the special-value-branch sample share falls and the vector conversion addresses carry the samples.

expected_signals.signal: vle16.v/vfwcvt.f.f.v/vse32.v instructions appear in decode_vector annotations.
The scalar per-element special-value branches (beqz subnormal/zero at 0x38968e and beq inf/nan at 0x389694) and the fmv.w.x/fsub.s/fmv.x.w round-trip disappear from the decode_vector hot loop.
Samples at the scalar bit-decode addresses 0x389676-0x38969c (slliw/and/addw/or) decrease toward zero.
decode_vector instruction and branch counts per call decrease.
QT_fp16 sql2_recons_error stays at ~1.448e-6 and ndiff_for_idempotence stays 0.

success_criteria: decode_vector disassembly main loop contains vle16.v + vfwcvt.f.f.v + vse32.v and no per-element special-value branches.
Per-element instruction count drops from ~15-17 scalar instructions to a few vector instructions amortized over 8+ FP16 elements (zvl128b e16).
QuantizerFP16 metrics stay exactly at baseline: QT_fp16 sql2_recons_error = 0.00000144839 and ndiff_for_idempotence = 0.
No regression for short d input vectors (path-selection threshold behaves).

controls: Keep the scalar decode_vector as the base implementation and add the RVV path strictly behind __riscv_v && __riscv_zvfhmin guards.
Verify the dispatch selects the RVV path on riscv64 and the NONE path on rv64gc (no v) builds, compiling both.
Gate on the same exhaustive bit-pattern parity check used for the fast-path guidance.
reasons: A new specialization that mis-gates could break non-vector or other-arch builds that must keep using the generic NONE path.
Interface/assertion consistency: AVX2 asserts d%8==0 and AVX512 d%16==0; an RVV path must define its own alignment/multiple contract or tail handling to stay general.
Reconstruction bit-flags (NaN/denorm) from a hardware conversion must be vetted against decode_fp16 before shipping, or sq-accuracy metrics drift.

conditions.description: riscv64 SIMD dispatch currently instantiates SIMDLevel::NONE for QuantizerFP16 decode (only x86 AVX2/AVX512 specializations exist in sq-avx2.cpp / sq-avx512-impl.h).
Build and runtime expose v + zvfhmin.
QuantizerFP16 decode is reached with d a multiple of the FP16 element count where vectorization pays, or the specialization handles the tail scalar.

actions.proposal: Add an RVV-enabled QuantizerFP16 decode specialization to the faiss scalar_quantizer dispatch so riscv64 builds no longer default decode_vector to the SIMDLevel::NONE scalar body: introduce a QuantizerFP16 (or decode_vector) path selected under __riscv_v && __riscv_zvfhmin that performs vle16/vfwcvt.f.f.v/vse32 widening conversion, modeled on the existing AVX2/AVX512 reconstruct_8_components specializations, with a scalar fallback for other builds.

correctness_checks: Confirm dispatch picks the RVV path on riscv64-with-v and the scalar path on a no-v build.
Re-run sq-accuracy and compare sql2_recons_error and ndiff_for_idempotence against baseline.
Build both -march configurations and diff the affected decode disassembly.

expected_signals.signal: An RVV QuantizerFP16 decode specialization (or RVV dispatch branch) appears in libfaiss and is selected on riscv64.
decode_vector annotate on the riscv64 build no longer shows the pure scalar SIMDLevel::NONE branchy body.
decode_vector instructions and branches per element decrease on the riscv64 build.
QT_fp16 sql2_recons_error and ndiff_for_idempotence remain at baseline (no reconstruction drift).

Reconstruction metrics (QT_fp16 sql2_recons_error, ndiff_for_idempotence) remain at baseline.

gaps.description: Only 3 cpu-clock samples were captured for the entire decode_vector function across the run, so the function's dynamic hotspot share within sq-accuracy and any benefit upper bound are weakly measured; per-call instruction count is known from disassembly but per-call cycle cost is not.

Runtime hardware ISA beyond the build tags is unverified: metadata provides Tag_RISCV_arch proving the build enables v1p0+zvfhmin, but no /proc/cpuinfo isa line or hwprobe evidence confirms the benchmark host actually executes v and zvfhmin.

The call context of decode_vector inside sq-accuracy is not evidenced (which benchmark phase generated the 3 samples, and how many reconstruction calls occurred), so end-to-end benchmark benefit of a vector decode cannot be quantified.

review_items.description: Capture a decode-heavy perf annotate/stat (e.g. bench_scalar_quantizer_distance or a large reconstruction workload) to obtain per-function samples, branch counts, and cycle attribution for decode_vector.
Collect /proc/cpuinfo isa or riscv_hwprobe (RISCV_HWPROBE_EXT_ZVFHMIN) on the benchmark host before relying on the vector fast path.
Perf record with call-graph (-g) over sq-accuracy to attribute decode_vector callers and call counts.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Measurement sparsity: only 3 cpu-clock samples were captured for the whole function across the run, so decode_vector may contribute a small absolute share of sq-accuracy runtime even though it is locally hot; benchmark-level impact of fixing it is not directly measured.

A pure memory-bound reading of the lhu/sw hotspots is weakened: the loop executes ~13-15 arithmetic/bitwise/branch instructions around each FP16 load and FP32 store, L1_dcache_load_miss_rate is only 0.317% over unit-stride sequential access, and the sampled addresses sit in the conversion instruction stream, not at cache-miss stalls.

A compiler-autovectorization-shortcoming (codegen) framing as the sole cause is refuted: on riscv64 the build routinely instantiates SIMDLevel::NONE and the transform is a precision-conversion identifier, so the ISA-extension routing assigns the cause to the operator_rvv precision-conversion pattern, not to a standalone codegen instruction-shape defect.

findings.conclusion: QuantizerFP16<SIMDLevel::NONE>::decode_vector is bottlenecked by a scalar, branch-per-lane software FP16->FP32 conversion loop: it inlines decode_fp16 (fp16-inl.h) as integer bit-decode that per element loads the FP16 halfword (lhu 0x389672), isolates exponent/sign with shifts and ANDs, branches on the zero/subnormal and inf/nan special cases (including the fmv.w.x/fsub.s/fmv.x.w float round-trip at 0x389658-0x389666), ORs the sign, and stores FP32 (sw 0x38969e); all three sampled addresses are inside this body, while the build ISA (v1p0+zvfhmin, zvl128b) provides the RVV widening conversion vfwcvt.f.f.v that the loop omits.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Generic scalar-main-loop row is superseded: the loop is a recognized FP16->FP32 precision-conversion (decode_fp16 branchy integer decode), and the no_vectorization row's own exclusionSummary routes operator-semantic precision conversion to the specific operator row.
The main work is a dtype conversion with per-lane special-value branches, not same-type add/subtract/multiply/compare elementwise arithmetic; conversion semantics route to precision conversion.
No activations, transcendental, piecewise or mask-based element functions appear; decode_fp16 is pure bit-level IEEE conversion.

No planar/interleave/block packing, channel reordering, bit-field or low-bit decomposition is performed; the FP16->FP32 widening is numeric conversion and each output occupies a distinct 4-byte FP32 slot.
There is no accumulator, sum/mean, dot-product or Hamming reduction; output count equals input count 1:1 with no cross-lane aggregation.
Accesses are fully unit-stride contiguous (code + 2*i, out + 4*i); there is no lookup table, data-dependent index, or runtime offset.
No M/N/K loop, FMA accumulation chain, or GEMV microkernel exists; conversion is the entire kernel, not an input step dominated by FP arithmetic.
No INT4/INT8 decode, zero-point handling, widening MAC, or integer requantization contract; precision conversion is the whole loop body.

findings.reasoning: Annotate shows the decode loop executing ~15 instructions plus 3 branches per element with no vector instruction; fp16-inl.h confirms decode_fp16 handles per-lane special values with conditional selects; fp16.h resolves to the fp16-inl fallback on riscv64 (no __F16C__/__aarch64__); metadata Tag_RISCV_arch proves v1p0+zvfhmin in the build, and isa-extensions.md routes v-present FP16-to-FP32 conversion to rvv_precision_conversion_kernels (vfwcvt.f.f.v fast path). Shared sample evidence: lhu, sw, addi each 33.33%.

alternative_explanations.explanation: SIMDLevel::NONE is the designed generic fallback for any architecture without an SSE/AVX port, so selecting it on RISC-V is expected dispatch behavior rather than a local defect; the real gap is the missing RVV implementation, which is exactly the claimed missing-specialization factor.

One could argue decode_vector call volume in sq-accuracy is too low for a specialization to matter (3 samples, 20 iterations), but the missing-specialization factor is still real for any reconstruction-heavy workload even if this testcase bounds the observable impact.

findings.conclusion: faiss ships no RISC-V vector specialization of the FP16 quantizer decode: QuantizerFP16 has only the generic SIMDLevel::NONE scalar template (used here) plus x86-intrinsic AVX2 and AVX512 specializations (reconstruct_8_components via _mm_cvtph_ps / AVX512), so on riscv64 neither the vector conversion vfwcvt.f.f.v nor any RVV widen path is ever engaged for decode_vector, guaranteeing the branchy scalar loop.
findings.reasoning: quantizers.h defines QuantizerFP16<SIMDLevel::NONE>::decode_vector as a plain per-element decode_fp16 loop and lets higher SIMDLevels inherit from NONE unless specialized; sq-avx2.cpp and sq-avx512-impl.h define the only SIMD specializations of QuantizerFP16, both behind x86 intrinsics; no RVV .cpp specialization exists in the scalar_quantizer directory search results; metadata confirms the riscv64 build arch and v+zvfhmin ISA.

asm.reason: No hand-written .S implementation participates in the measured decode path. The annotated loop is compiler-generated from QuantizerFP16<SIMDLevel::NONE>::decode_vector (quantizers.h) calling decode_fp16 (fp16-inl.h); SIMD specializations exist only as x86 AVX2/AVX512 intrinsics (sq-avx2.cpp), no RISC-V assembly exists, and no policy-mandated missing .S kernel evidence was found.

codegen.reason: The scalar-compiled decode_fp16 loop cost is dominated by per-element bit manipulation plus fixed-width data movement; the ISA-extension routing table directs v-present precision-conversion work to operator_rvv rvv_precision_conversion_kernels, and no dispatch, synchronization, or instruction-shape limit separable from that scalar-loop inefficiency is evidenced.

crypto.reason: decode_vector performs IEEE FP16->FP32 bit re-encoding (fp16-inl.h decode_fp16); no cryptographic arithmetic, cipher mode, hash, checksum, or binary-field work is present.

offload.reason: No GEMM/matrix-engine/parallel offload opportunity is evidenced; elementwise precision conversion is a lane-independent operator and is routed by the ISA-extension table to the operator RVV precision-conversion pattern, not to the offload row.

operator_rvv.reason: Scalar lane-independent FP16->FP32 conversion loop dominates the function: per-element lhu, shifts, and-branches, sw at 0x389672/0x38969e/0x3896a0. Build ISA includes v1p0 + zvfhmin enabling the proven lane-independent RVV formulation vfwcvt.f.f.v (widening FP16->FP32), and the isa-extensions routing maps v-present builds to rvv_precision_conversion_kernels.

runtime_os.reason: No timer, interrupt, privilege-boundary, or runtime context-management code is present in decode_vector; the loop is pure user-mode elementwise conversion.

string_memory.reason: Memory access is only the per-element FP16 load / FP32 store inside a numeric precision conversion; no string, memcpy, compare/checksum, or sentinel-scan semantics apply, so memory-copy/sentinel/compare rows are not candidates.

vectorized_tuning.reason: No existing compiler-generated RVV code exists in this function; the annotated body is fully scalar, so vector-configuration/bookkeeping tuning rows (register budget, operand form, vsetvl management) have nothing to tune.

summary.observed_anomaly: QuantizerFP16<SIMDLevel::NONE>::decode_vector is bottlenecked by a scalar, branch-per-lane software FP16->FP32 conversion loop: it inlines decode_fp16 (fp16-inl.h) as integer bit-decode that per element loads the FP16 halfword (lhu 0x389672), isolates exponent/sign with shifts and ANDs, branches on the zero/subnormal and inf/nan special cases (including the fmv.w.x/fsub.s/fmv.x.w float round-trip at 0x389658-0x389666), ORs the sign, and stores FP32 (sw 0x38969e); all three sampled addresses are inside this body, while the build ISA (v1p0+zvfhmin, zvl128b) provides the RVV widening conversion vfwcvt.f.f.v that the loop omits.
